ops.body:
P2 of the cc-pool × synckit plan (2026-07-08) landed the sync engine, then ran four adversarial reviews (2× gpt-5.5/codex, 2× fable) against its two core invariants. Both were refuted; the fixes below are load-bearing. Inline comments in the code are deliberately terse — this doc is the rationale.

## Stamp discipline: forceStamp vs bumpStamp (service.go)

cregistry is an LWW-element-set: Add/Remove adopt a stamp only when strictly newer than the entry's current field, Present = Added > Removed (tie ⇒ removed). Two stamp helpers encode WHO may assert presence:

- **forceStamp** = max(now, Added+1, Removed+1). Explicit user intents only: PublishAccount (add/relogin), RecordLabel (rename), RecordRemoval (remove). A deliberate action observed the entry and MUST land, over any skew-ahead peer stamp — including flipping tombstones (PublishAccount) and landing removals under skew (RecordRemoval; a bare wall stamp below a peer-skewed Added advances Removed yet leaves the entry Present: a remove that reports success and tears down nothing anywhere — critical finding, fable-tombstone #2/codex-tombstone #1).
- **bumpStamp** = max(Added, Removed)+1, no wall clock. ALL automatic mutations: ClaimHolder, RenewLease, ReleaseLease, NoteCredWrite, ScanPublish folds. Critical finding (fable-tombstone #1): with wall-forced stamps, any routine mutation on a host that had not yet merged a tombstone re-asserted presence at wall time and permanently cancelled the removal pool-wide — and "remove while busy on a peer" is the standard deferred-teardown case, with the busy peer renewing its lease every ≤25min. Bump stamps still land locally (by construction they exceed the observed entry) and still win value-LWW against peers on the same base, but any later-in-real-time removal beats them at merge.

Accepted residuals: a rename (wall-forced, explicit intent) concurrent with an unmerged removal is a genuine intent conflict — either LWW outcome is defensible. Equal-stamp ties resolve by canonical-JSON comparison (domain-blind, synckit cregistry); single-holder discipline makes collisions rare and damage is registry-only, healed by the next note/scan fold.

## Chain lineage: ParentHash ordering (value.go, credpull.go, driver.go, credinstall.go, usage.go)

Critical finding (fable-staler #1): ExpiresAt is minted from the LOCAL wall clock (oauth.go: Expiry = now.Add(expires_in)) — NOT server-issued, so it is not skew-immune, contrary to the original plan's risk analysis. With cross-host skew exceeding the gap between two rotations on different hosts, every strictly-later-expiry gate agreed the spent PARENT chain was "fresher" than its live child: the registry no-oped the child's publication, the parent was re-installed over the child, and the next refresh POSTed an already-spent refresh token → invalid_grant → needs-login, with refresh-token-reuse family-revocation risk.

Fix: refresh chains are LINEAR (each credential is minted by spending its parent's refresh token), so freshness is lineage-first, expiry-fallback:
- ChainStamp.ParentHash = CredentialHash of the spent parent (CredentialHash lives in internal/creds: length-prefixed SHA-256 of the token pair — a one-way digest, not a secret).
- accounts.cred_hash / cred_parent_hash persist the local chain position; writeCred (the single write funnel, CAS included) maintains them and passes the resolved parent to OnCredWrite; AdoptRotatedToken resolves parent = previously recorded cred_hash (a session rotation's parent is the last chain we wrote; an adopt of an unchanged credential preserves recorded lineage).
- Child-of-X beats X at every layer regardless of expiry: NoteCredWrite lands a child of the advertised chain; ScanPublish folds when the registry advertises our parent and never regresses onto a chain that is our child; the driver pulls when the registry chain is our local's child; FetchCredential accepts a child envelope; InstallSyncedCredential installs a child of current and REFUSES anything matching the recorded parent (the we-are-ahead guard that closes the pre-note window).
Known transient: a skew-ahead laggard's note can still briefly regress the registry via the expiry fallback; the install-side parent-refusal protects every host's live child and the child holder's next note/scan re-advances it. No credential can be destroyed.

## Holder-ahead halt (credpull.go errHolderAhead)

Critical finding (codex-staler #1): the fetch hash gate pins the envelope to the registry's advertised chain, so in the async-mirror lag window after every rotation the healthy HOLDER's fresher answer was rejected (hash mismatch) and the fallback accepted a laggard's exact-match copy of the advertised chain — whose refresh token the holder had already spent. Installing it invalid_grants on the next refresh. Fix: a holder answering self-consistent-and-strictly-fresher-than-advertised proves the registry itself is stale → the pull halts as the normal deferred outcome (no laggard consulted); the registry catches up (mirror note or scan fold) and the next tick pulls cleanly. An unhealthy holder (older or self-inconsistent answer) still falls back.

## Install funnel = CAS (credinstall.go)

fable-staler #2: cc-pool's account lock does not bind the claude binary — `claude /login` writes the keychain item lock-free (the e1bb18ed incident rationale, ccn 064315a). InstallSyncedCredential therefore writes through writeCredCAS with the compared credential's access token as baseline: an underfoot login aborts the install as a clean skip.

## Teardown contract (service.go teardown)

Fail-closed and per-item isolated: busy or unprovable-idle defers (nil Sessions seam ⇒ defers everything — P2 ships intentionally inert until the P3 wiring); per-item resolve/remove failures log and defer (one broken account must not starve the sweep — map order picked the victims; codex-tombstone #2); ambiguous uuid resolution (>1 local row sharing the uuid) is refused outright — a tombstone must never serially destroy every row sharing a uuid (fable-tombstone #4); after TryClaim the registry is re-loaded and a now-Present entry (explicit re-add since the pass snapshot) is spared — destroying it would eat a fresh login whose chain exists nowhere else (fable-tombstone #3). Only a registry load failure is fatal, matching Converge's per-item contract.

## Takeover threshold (syncgate.go)

takeoverStaleAfter = 35min, deliberately past the 900s synckitd reconcile tick + a converge pass: a dropped mirror event (bounded queue, never blocks writeCred) leaves a LIVE holder advertising an expired chain with stale RotatedAt — exactly the dead-holder signature — until its next scan-publish heals the registry. A shorter threshold let a takeover double-spend a healthy holder's chain inside that window (fable-staler #4).

## P3 obligations (also recorded in the plan's P2-synthesis amendments)

Enable backfill uses ScanPublish, never PublishAccount (bulk publish resurrects peers' removals). Re-add publishes BEFORE SetAccountUUID. Doctor: registry.json load-health (corrupt file ⇒ chronic fail-open refresh gate) + uuid-dupe warning (dupes wedge teardown by design). Daemon wiring must set svc.Sessions alongside svc.Claims, Server.sync, Server.syncPull, Manager.OnCredWrite=mirror.Hook, mirror.Run, startSyncServer. The Manager-backed Locals adapter must set Chain.ParentHash from Account.CredParentHash.

Accepted residuals not fixed by design: deleted registry.json on a host holding deferred-teardown accounts resurrects removals (indistinguishable from first enable); cregistry equal-stamp JSON tiebreak is domain-blind.
## P3 review addendum (2026-07-08)

A fifth adversarial pass (gpt-5.5) reviewed the P3 lifecycle hooks. Fixed: the `ccp status` TUI re-login paths now run the same publish tail as `ccp login` (tuiFinishRelogin/tuiCheckFresh → afterReloginIO), and runRelogin's short-circuit publish is pinned by test. Reviewed and REJECTED: "Publish unconditionally sets Chain.Holder=self without takeover-style gating." Holder names who holds the ADVERTISED chain, and a publish only follows a proven-live local chain (fresh /login or forced-refresh rotation) that no other host possesses — takeover preconditions would gate the one host that can actually refresh it. A parallel login never revokes a peer's chain (independent OAuth sessions; the same fact that makes credential adoption impossible), so the displaced holder's chain stays live, its session lease is preserved by the publish, and holdership self-corrects on that peer's next rotation note. The transient Holder/Lease split is benign: ranking penalizes by lease, teardown defers by Sessions, and takeover is blocked by the live lease.

## Relogin & credential-liveness rationale (comment-sweep append, 2026-07-08)

- afterRelogin's DropDivergentCopy is hygiene, not correctness: a cross-session re-login (e.g. an SSH login of a Keychain-backed account) lands the fresh credential in the FILE backend, stranding a stale copy on the other backend. Resolution already prefers the fresher copy (probeCredentialStores fresher-wins), so the drop only prevents doctor noise and future ambiguity.
- shortCircuitRelogin proves liveness ONLY by a forced refresh because the daemon sets needs-login on PROACTIVE refresh failure: an access token can carry hours of validity on a chain whose refresh token is already revoked. That counterexample is what killed the usage-probe liveness design (a 200 from /usage proves nothing about the refresh chain).
